record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: In open dynamical systems, including billiards with distortion, nonuniform hyperbolicity, or no hyperbolicity, how should the position of a hole be chosen in order to maximize or minimize escape, where the measure of escape may be the escape rate γ, the full survival probability function P(t), or another suitably defined escape statistic?

evidence.quote: Another important question posed in this work is that of optimisation: how to choose a hole position to minimise or maximise escape, for example γ or even the whole function P(t) [1, 18].
Open problem 3. Optimisation: Specify where to place a hole to maximise or minimise a suitably defined measure of escape.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, T, \mu)$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system, where $T : M \to M$ is a (possibly non-uniformly hyperbolic, or distorted, or non-hyperbolic) map and $\mu$ is an invariant probability measure. Given a measurable subset $H \subset M$ called the "hole", define the survival set up to time $t$ by
$$S_t(H) = \{ x \in M : T^k(x) \notin H \text{ for all } 0 \le k \le t \},$$
and let the survival probability function be $P_H(t) = \mu(S_t(H))$. When the limit exists, define the escape rate through the hole $H$ by
$$\gamma(H) = -\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log P_H(t).$$
The setting includes the case where $T$ is the billiard map associated with a planar billiard table (possibly with distortion, non-uniform hyperbolicity, or no hyperbolicity), and $H$ is a small region of the phase space (e.g., an arc on the boundary).

Problem. Consider a class $\mathcal{H}$ of admissible holes (for instance, all holes of a fixed $\mu$-measure $\varepsilon > 0$). Determine, in terms of the dynamics of $T$ and the geometry of $M$:
(a) which holes $H^* \in \mathcal{H}$ maximize the escape rate $\gamma(H)$, and which minimize it;
(b) more generally, which holes maximize or minimize the survival probability function $P_H(t)$ (for all $t$, or pointwise in $t$), or another suitably defined statistic of escape.
Provide a characterization of optimal hole positions covering systems with distortion, non-uniform hyperbolicity, and the absence of hyperbolicity.
artifact.status_search_result: For strongly chaotic (uniformly hyperbolic) systems with small holes, partial results characterize hole-position effects: e.g., faster escape through holes containing a periodic point of minimal period (Bunimovich–Yurchenko and follow-ups), and there are escape-rate formulas via periodic orbits. However, for general open systems with distortion, non-uniform hyperbolicity, or no hyperbolicity, a complete characterization of optimal hole placement remains open; recent works (e.g., on intermittent maps with shrinking holes, physical billiards) continue to address special cases.

status_evidence.title: Where to place a hole to achieve a maximal escape rate
status_evidence.snippet: For holes of equal size in strongly chaotic maps, faster escape occurs through a hole containing a periodic point of minimal period.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for uniformly hyperbolic systems linking optimal hole placement to short periodic orbits.

status_evidence.title: On the escape rate for intermittent maps with holes shrinking around the indifferent fixed point
status_evidence.snippet: Studies escape rate asymptotics for intermittent (non-uniformly hyperbolic) maps with holes around an indifferent fixed point.
status_evidence.claim: Hole-placement and escape-rate questions in non-uniformly hyperbolic settings are still being actively investigated.

status_evidence.title: Why Escape Is Faster Than Expected
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates how specific dynamical features near a hole affect the escape rate, beyond merely its measure.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works further explore how hole position influences escape, indicating the general problem is not fully resolved.
